plan.concept: How the RANSAC algorithm robustly estimates models by ignoring outlier data points that corrupt standard fitting techniques.
learningObjectives: Identify the difference between inliers (points following the true underlying trend) and outliers (spurious data points).
Explain why standard least-squares regression is highly sensitive to outliers and yields incorrect results.
Describe how RANSAC uses random minimal subsets and consensus thresholds to find a robust model.
plan.keyInsight: Instead of trying to accommodate every data point, RANSAC finds the 'truth' by repeatedly guessing models using minimal random samples and choosing the one that gets the most votes from the rest of the dataset.

interactions.label: Fitting Method
interactions.effect: Switches between showing a standard Least-Squares regression line and the iterative RANSAC algorithm visualization.
interactions.teaches: The fundamental difference between holistic algorithms that get pulled by noise, and robust, consensus-based algorithms.

interactions.label: RANSAC Iteration
interactions.effect: Cycles through different random 2-point selections, showing the generated hypothesis line and its corresponding 'inlier' points within a colored tolerance band.
interactions.teaches: How random selection can yield poor models initially, but iteratively guarantees finding a model that aligns with the majority of the data.

demo_steps.title: Analyze the Raw Data
demo_steps.narration: Look at these 11 data points. You can easily spot a clear upward linear trend from left to right, but notice the two isolated points on the bottom-right and top-right that completely deviate from this trend—these are our outliers.
demo_steps.focus: The spatial distribution of the scatter plot points, distinguishing the linear main cluster from the two outliers on the right.

demo_steps.title: The Least Squares Failure
demo_steps.narration: With 'Fitting Method' set to Least Squares, notice how the fitted line is pulled downward and skewed by the outliers. Standard optimization tries to minimize the distance to ALL points, meaning even a few bad outliers completely ruin the model accuracy.
demo_steps.focus: The fitted Least-Squares line, showing how it fails to align with either the main trend or the outliers.

demo_steps.title: RANSAC: Bad Random Sample
demo_steps.narration: Now let's switch to RANSAC. In this iteration, the algorithm randomly picks just two points (highlighted in red) to draw a trial line. Because one of the picked points is an outlier, the resulting line is terrible, and only 3 total points fall within the shaded consensus threshold band.
demo_steps.focus: The two red-highlighted sample points, the trial line, and the narrow tolerance band containing very few green 'inlier' points.

demo_steps.title: RANSAC: Finding Consensus
demo_steps.narration: As we cycle to a later iteration, RANSAC happens to select two points that both belong to the main linear trend. Look at how many points now fall inside the shaded consensus band! This model receives 9 'votes' (inliers) out of 11.
demo_steps.focus: The newly selected trial points along the main trend line, with a large majority of the scatter points turning green to indicate consensus.

demo_steps.title: The Robust Final Fit
demo_steps.narration: RANSAC selects the model with the highest consensus, then refines it using only those inliers. Compare this final line to the skewed Least-Squares line from Step 2: RANSAC has successfully ignored the outliers completely to discover the true underlying relationship.
demo_steps.focus: The final refined line passing perfectly through the main group of points, leaving the outliers colored red outside the consensus zone.

plan.reconstructionNotes: An interactive scatter plot with an X and Y axis (no numerical values, just arrows as in the original image). Plot about 11 circular points: 9 forming a noisy linear trend sloping upwards from bottom-left to top-center, and 2 distinct outliers positioned on the right side of the plot area (one near the bottom, one near the top-right). Standard Least-Squares mode should render a single blue line pulled away from the main trend by the outliers. RANSAC mode should highlight two 'sampled' points in red, draw a dashed trial line through them, show a semi-transparent colored tolerance band (envelope) around the line, and color all points inside the band green (inliers) and points outside red (outliers). Step through 5 distinct RANSAC iterations: Iteration 1-3 show poor random fits (including outliers), Iteration 4 shows a good fit of the main cluster, and Iteration 5 shows the final optimized fit using only the consensus inliers.
